answer: A newcomer enters through one narrow inlet and starts in a shared meadow of small starter jobs strangers actually need, each checked by the stranger who used the result. Standing grows only through a spiral audit: every season strangers re-check a random sample of the agent's old deals, digging deeper each round, and privileges rise only while the old work still holds up. A farm fails because its fakes share one shallow history, so one audit of the same scripted deals collapses the whole cluster at once, and each exposed account must redo fresh stranger-checked work alone to re-enter.
